title: Ajit Properties v. Shyam Textiles
text: The landlord-company, Ajit Properties, seeks eviction of the tenant, Shyam Textiles, from commercial premises under the Delhi Rent Control Act. The ground is non-payment of rent and bonafide requirement for the landlord's own business. The tenancy has been in existence since 2001. The tenant argues protection under the Delhi Rent Control Act as a protected tenant. The court examined the standard rent fixed under the Act and found that the tenant had been paying below the permissible standard rent for the last 36 months, constituting arrears of rent. Additionally, the landlord established that it intends to wind down its warehousing operations and use the suit premises for its retail showroom, which amounts to bona fide requirement under the Rent Control Act. Eviction is decreed on both grounds. Possession to be handed over within four months. Arrears of rent to be settled as directed.
